newsitem.title: USA: US SPOT NATGAS REBOUNDS WITH FUTURES, STORAGE BUYS.
newsitem.headline: US SPOT NATGAS REBOUNDS WITH FUTURES, STORAGE BUYS.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices regained their strength Monday as buyers re-emerged after the weekend for storage supplies and the futures market staged another rally, traders said.
NYMEX's September contract soared to another new high of $2.605, up 10.2 cents from Friday's settlement.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, swing prices at the Henry Hub recovered an average of 15 cents to the low-$2.50s.
In the Midwest, swing prices regained 20 cents to the mid-$2.40s. Chicago city-gate gas prices were quoted at $2.58-2.62.
In the Permian Basin market, prices also rose an average of 20 cents to $2.40-2.48, while Waha values were quoted at $2.43-2.53.
San Juan basin gas sold at $2.35-2.42, traders said, indicating a gain of about 15 cents from Friday's levels.

Southern California border prices soared into the low-$2.60s early but then settled into the mid-to-high $2.50s shortly before nomination deadlines. Temperatures in the western part of the Southwest were expected to remain five to 10-degrees above normal this week, but some northern California buyers reportedly turned back some gas, thereby putting some pressure on the market late in trading.

In the East, prices at the New York city gate returned to the low-$2.70s, up about 20 cents from Friday. Traders said large volumes of gas were most likely being injected into storage early this week as cooler-than-normal weather continued in the region.
